facts.fact_text: The three applicants in the present case were involved in a number of public events in 2007-2008 in Rostov-na-Donu.

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a meeting of approximately three hundred participants on Sovetov Square from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 30 June 2007.

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold the 'Dissenters' March' (Марш несогласных) along Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets following the meeting on Sovetov Square on 30 June 2007.
On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold another meeting at Karl Marx Square until 7.30 p.m. on 30 June 2007.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin proceeded with the static demonstration (picket).
On 8 December 2008 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a picket on Russian Constitution Day (12 December 2008).
At 5.20 p.m. on 12 December 2008 Mr Nagibin came to Voroshilovskiy Drive for a solitary demonstration.
Mr Nagibin carried a sandwich board during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin distributed leaflets to passers-by during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the location of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the time of conduct of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the manner of conduct of several public events.

The Rostov-na-Donu town administration replied to Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. stating that if they intended to campaign for candidates of the association not listed on the electoral ballots they would violate the law.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin proceeded with the static demonstration (picket).

On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin was apprehended because his passport was found to be defiled with unauthorised pen writing and the police officers intended to draft the relevant record of the administrative offence at the police station.
Mr Nagibin refused to follow the police officers to the police station, explaining that he was a participant in the picket.
Mr Nagibin was brought to a police station and charged with non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

On 2 December 2007 Mr Nagibin was convicted of the administrative offence of non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer on the basis of the police report and oral testimony of officer Mr Kh.
Mr Nagibin was apprehended on 24 November 2007 and brought to the Kirovskiy district police station in Rostov-na-Donu.
Mr Nagibin stayed at the Kirovskiy district police station in Rostov-na-Donu from 24 November 2007 until 26 November 2007.
On 26 November 2007 Mr Nagibin was brought before the Justice of the Peace of the Kirovskiy District.
On 26 November 2007 the Justice of the Peace of the Kirovskiy District adjourned the hearing in Mr Nagibin's case.
Mr Nagibin was released on 26 November 2007 following the adjournment of the hearing.
When convicting Mr Nagibin of an administrative offence, the judge sentenced him to three days' imprisonment.
The judge held that Mr Nagibin's detention from 5.20 p.m. on 24 November 2007 to 10.45 a.m. on 26 November 2007 should be credited to the time to be served.

On an unspecified date Mr Nagibin brought a judicial complaint against the Kirovskiy district police station arguing that the period from 3.10 p.m. until 5.20 p.m. on 24 November 2007 (the time from his factual arrest until his transfer to the police station was completed) should be included in the period of his detention.

Mr Nagibin argued that the period from 10.45 a.m. until 5.20 p.m. on 26 November 2007 (the time when he was transferred to the judge and waited for the hearing) should also be included in the period of his detention.
On 14 March 2008 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu rejected Mr Nagibin's complaint against the Kirovskiy district police station.

The Pervomayskiy District Court noted that the Code of Administrative Offences distinguished between 'transfer' (Article 27.2 § 1, 'доставление') — the act of transfer by convoy of an individual to a police station to prepare a report on an administrative offence — and 'administrative detention' (Article 27.3 § 1, 'административное задержание') — a short-time restriction on the liberty of the offender for the purpose of correct and diligent examination of the administrative case.

Relying on the testimony of police officers, the Pervomayskiy District Court found that Mr Nagibin had been subjected to 'transfer' until 5.20 p.m. on 24 November 2007 and had been free to move around the police station and had not been held there by force.

The Pervomayskiy District Court found that on 26 November 2007 Mr Nagibin had not been restricted in his liberty while on the premises of the Justice of the Peace and had been able to confer with his lawyer and other individuals.
On 23 April 2008 the Rostov Regional Court upheld the Pervomayskiy District Court's judgment of 14 March 2008, reproducing its text verbatim.

From 24 to 26 November 2007 Mr Nagibin (the applicant in application no. 10460/09) was held in the administrative-detention cell located on the premises of the Kirovskiy district police station in Rostov-na-Donu.
The administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station measured 3.5 square metres.
Mr Nagibin shared the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station with three to five other detainees.
The administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station was equipped with one bed, thirty centimetres wide and too short for an adult.
Detainees in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station took turns to sleep on the floor.
There was no natural light in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station.
There was no possibility for outdoor exercise for detainees held in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station.
Mr Nagibin complained before the domestic courts about the poor conditions of his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station from 24 to 26 November 2007.
On 27 May 2010 the Rostov Regional Court found that Mr Nagibin was unlawfully deprived of proper meals during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station from 24 to 26 November 2007.
On 27 May 2010 the Rostov Regional Court found that Mr Nagibin was unlawfully deprived of a sleeping place during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station from 24 to 26 November 2007.
The domestic courts established that Mr Nagibin was kept in a cell measuring 3.5 square metres with three other persons during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station.
On 8 December 2008 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a picket on Russian Constitution Day (12 December 2008).
At 5.20 p.m. on 12 December 2008 Mr Nagibin came to Voroshilovskiy Drive for a solitary demonstration.
Mr Nagibin carried a sandwich board during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin distributed leaflets to passers-by during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
At approximately 5.40 p.m. on 12 December 2008 two police officers apprehended Mr Nagibin during his solitary demonstration at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin was taken to the Kirovskiy district police station following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.

Mr Nagibin was charged with a breach of public order and verbal assaults, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.
The administrative arrest record stated that Mr Nagibin had been arrested to ensure administrative trial, identify the offender and to draft the administrative offence record.
Mr Nagibin noted in the administrative arrest record that he had been in a solo demonstration when the police arrested him and contested the lawfulness of the arrest.

On 13 December 2008 the Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District found Mr Nagibin guilty of breach of public order and verbal assaults under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District based the conviction on submissions by several witnesses and two police officers, establishing in general terms that Mr Nagibin had used foul language in a public space.
The text of the judgment of 13 December 2008 did not specify which particular words Mr Nagibin had pronounced.

The Justice of the Peace did not address Mr Nagibin's arguments that he had not used foul language but rather had been making a solo demonstration when the police officers came and ordered him to stop the unlawful demonstration.
The Justice of the Peace sentenced Mr Nagibin to three days' administrative imprisonment, to be calculated from 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008.
Mr Nagibin appealed against his conviction of 13 December 2008, arguing inter alia that the judge had not taken into account the fact that he had been picketing.
On 12 January 2009 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu upheld Mr Nagibin's conviction of 13 December 2008.
On 25 March 2009 the Pervomayskiy District Court rejected Mr Nagibin's claim for inclusion of the time period from 5.48 p.m. to 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008 in the period of his detention.
The Pervomayskiy District Court held on 25 March 2009 that it was not reliably shown that Mr Nagibin had been detained at 5.48 p.m. on 12 December 2008.
On 28 May 2009 the Rostov Regional Court upheld the Pervomayskiy District Court's decision of 25 March 2009 on appeal.

On 22 June 2007 the Justice of the Peace of the 4th Circuit of the Pervomayskiy District of Rostov-na-Donu found Mr Nagibin guilty of a breach of public order, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
At about 3 p.m. on 12 December 2006 Mr Nagibin was apprehended by police officers from the Organised Crime Unit of the Rostov Regional Police Directorate as he was leaving his home.
The police officers from the Organised Crime Unit of the Rostov Regional Police Directorate brought Mr Nagibin to the Pervomayskiy district police station on 12 December 2006.
According to the police, Mr Nagibin was stopped on 12 December 2006 for an identity check.
According to the police, Mr Nagibin resisted the identity check and attempted to flee.

At the Pervomayskiy district police station, a report on an administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with lawful demands of a police officer) was drawn up against Mr Nagibin.
Mr Nagibin remained in custody on the premises of the Pervomayskiy district police station until 3 p.m. on 13 December 2006.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that the police officers had acted within their competence because they had the right, under section 11 §§ 2 and 15 of the Police Act, to check the identity papers of individuals suspected of a criminal or administrative offence.

The Pervomayskiy District Court noted that the Code of Administrative Offences distinguished between 'transfer' (Article 27.2 § 1, 'доставление') — the act of transfer by convoy of an individual to a police station to prepare a report on an administrative offence — and 'administrative detention' (Article 27.3 § 1, 'административное задержание') — a short-time restriction on the liberty of the offender for the purpose of correct and diligent examination of the administrative case.

The Rostov-na-Donu town administration replied to Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. stating that if they intended to campaign for candidates of the association not listed on the electoral ballots they would violate the law.
On 20 June 2007 the Rostov-na-Donu town administration informed Mr Nagibin that the contemplated events had not been sufficiently prepared.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate which side of Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets the march would take place.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate where the participants would cross the streets.
On 21 September 2007 Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. complained to a court about the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's de facto refusal of their application to hold a march.

On 8 October 2007 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found in favour of Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. regarding the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's de facto refusal of their application to hold a march.
Following the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's appeal, on 21 November 2007 the Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court reversed the Pervomayskiy District Court's decision of 8 October 2007.

The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court held on 21 November 2007 that the administration's response had not prohibited the meeting or prevented the organisers from submitting more detailed information on its route and venue.
The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court held on 21 November 2007 that the organisers had not made use of the possibility to submit more detailed information on the route and venue.

The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court determined, without referring to specific dates, that Mr Nagibin, Mr Batyy and Mr Ye. had missed the three-month time-limit for appealing against the Rostov-na-Donu town administration's decision.
The applicant in application no. 42250/08 is Mr Nikolayev.
